Rashi on Shabbat 28a:1:1.hebrew: ממשכן - דלא הוה ביה שום יוצא מן העץ אלא פשתן, כדכתיב: עשר יריעות שש משזר:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:1:1.english: From the Tabernacle - For there was in it no [material] that emerges from a tree except linen, as it is written: "ten curtains of twisted fine linen" (Exodus 26:1).

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:1:2.hebrew: שזורין - דטור"ש בלע"ז, דכתיב משזר:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:1:2.english: Twisted - Destors [twisted] in Old French, as it is written: “Twisted” (Exodus 26:1).

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:1:3.hebrew: וחוטן כפול ששה - כדאמרינן בפ' בא לו דסדר יומא (דף עא:): דברים שנאמר בהן שש — חוטן כפול ששה. ואי קשיא: כיון דיליף ממשכן, כלים ואדם שתחת גג הבית, וכל שאר אהלים דלא דמו למשכן — מנלן דמטמו? בספרי תניא: מנין לעשות שאר המאהילים כאהל? אמרת: מה מצורע הקל עשה בו כל המאהיל כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:1:3.english: And their thread was folded sixfold - As we say in the chapter [entitled] Ba Lo of Tractate Yoma (71b): [Concerning] items about which shesh [fine linen] is stated, their thread is folded sixfold. And if it is difficult: Since he derives [tent] from the Tabernacle, [as for] vessels and a person who are under the roof of a house, and all other tents that do not resemble the Tabernacle — from where do we know that they become impure? In the Sifrei it is taught: From where [do we derive] to treat other overhanging [structures] like a tent? You say: Just as regarding a leper, which is lenient, [the Torah] made whatever overhangs [like a tent], etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:2:1.english: So too here, beams - And say that [what is made] of wood is also called a tent.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:2:2.hebrew: משכן קרוי משכן - כגון עשר יריעות שש משזר, ומשכן איקרי ״אהל״, דכתיב (שמות לט): ״את משכן אהל מועד״:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:2:2.english: The Tabernacle is called Tabernacle - Such as the ten curtains of fine twined linen; and the Tabernacle is called a tent, as it is written (Exodus 39:32): “The Tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting.”

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:2:3.hebrew: הכי נמי - דמכסה עורות לאו אהל, ולענין טומאה נמי לא מקבל:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:2:3.english: [Is it] so too - That the covering of skins is not a tent, and with regard to impurity, it too does not contract [impurity]?

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:2:4.english: Now, the hide of a kosher animal - Such as rams dyed red.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:2:5.hebrew: מה תחתון - עשתי עשרה יריעות עזים לאהל על המשכן. דמשכן היינו עשר יריעות המחוברות בקרסי זהב, מלמעלה מהן אהל יריעות עזים, ולמעלה מהן מכסה העורות:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:2:5.english: Just as the lower [covering] - [This refers to the] eleven curtains of goats' [hair, made] 'for a tent over the Tabernacle.' For 'Tabernacle' refers to the ten curtains connected with golden clasps; above them was the tent of goats' [hair] curtains, and above them was the covering of skins.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:3:1.hebrew: מאי קמיבעי ליה - הא ממשכן גמר לה ר' (אליעזר) לעיל בריש שמעתין, והתם טהורה היא דהוי למלאכת משכן:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:3:1.english: What is his dilemma? - Behold, Rabbi (Eliezer) derived it from the Tabernacle above at the beginning of our sugya, and there, it was a kosher [animal] that was [used] for the work of the Tabernacle.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:4:1.hebrew: מכסה אחד היה - חציו של אילים וחציו של תחשים. ולמעלה דקרא אתרוייהו כתיב — דבין אילים בין תחשים היה מכסה אחד מלמעלה לאהל יריעות העזים:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:4:1.english: There was one covering - Half of it was of rams’ [hides] and half of it was of teḥashim [hides]. And [the word] “above” in the verse is written concerning both of them — for whether [of] rams or [of] teḥashim, it was one covering from above over the tent of the goats’ [hair] curtains.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:4:2.english: Tela ilan - It is a non-kosher wild animal, and variegated with colors.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:4:3.english: If so - This is a support.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:4:4.english: That it rejoices - That it rejoices in its beauty, in [its] colors.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:5:1.hebrew: עור או בעור - גבי נגעים כתיב או בעור, והוה מצי למכתב או עור:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:5:1.english: “Hide,” “or in a hide” - Regarding leprosy, it is written: “or in a hide,” and it could have written: “or a hide.”

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:5:2.hebrew: ושלקה ביד כהן - משהראהו, ביד כהן נעשה נגע, ומתחלה לא היה נגע:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:5:2.english: And [a hide] that was afflicted in the hands of a priest - Once [the owner] showed it [to the priest], while in the priest's custody a lesion formed on the hide, whereas initially there was no lesion.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:5:3.english: [If] one cut from all of them - From all [those] mentioned in the verse, and joined them together.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:6:1.hebrew: שרצים מטמאין בכעדשה - ומת בכזית, ונגעים בכגריס, והוא פחות מכזית:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:6:1.english: Creeping animals transmit impurity with a lentil-bulk - And a corpse [transmits impurity] with an olive-bulk, and leprosy with [the size of] a split-bean, which is less than an olive-bulk.

Rashi on Shabbat 28a:6:2.hebrew: אף אני אביא אהל המת שעור טמא בו - כדאמר לעיל: מקיש עליון לתחתון, דקרוי אהל:
Rashi on Shabbat 28a:6:2.english: I will also bring a tent over a corpse, in which hide is ritually impure - As [the Gemara] said above: [The verse] juxtaposes the upper [covering] to the lower [covering], [establishing] that it is called a tent.

Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:1:1.hebrew: ויפרוש את האהל וגו' - תימה לר"י: מנא ליה דהאי אהל היינו שש משזר? אימא היינו יריעות עזים, דאשכחנא בהדיא דאיקרי אהל, כדכתיב: "ועשית יריעות עזים לאהל על המשכן"! וכן משמע פשטיה דקרא: "ויפרוש את האהל" — דהיינו יריעות עזים, "על המשכן" — דהיינו שש משזר, כדכתיב: "ואת המשכן תעשה עשר יריעות שש משזר"! ויש לומר: דדייק משום דקרא כתיב בהקמת המשכן, וחשיב לעיל בסדר הקמתן, דמתחלה נתן אדנים ואחר כך הקרשים, וכתיב אחר הקרשים: "ויפרוש את האהל" — משמע היינו יריעות התחתונות, שהם שש משזר, דהם תחלת הפרשה. ותימה: דאמאי לא יליף מהא דמשכן היינו יריעות שש משזר, כדכתיב: "ואת המשכן תעשה" וגו', ומשכן איקרי אהל, דכתיב: "את משכן אהל מועד"? ושמא אהאי קרא סמיך:
Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:1:1.english: “And he spread the tent,” etc. - The Ri finds it puzzling: From where does [the Gemara] know that this “tent” is [made of] fine twined linen? Say [instead] that this refers to the goats’ hair curtains, for we explicitly find that they are called a “tent,” as it is written: “And you shall make curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the Tabernacle” (Exodus 26:7)! And so indicates the plain meaning of the verse: “And he spread the tent” — meaning the goats’ hair curtains — “over the Tabernacle” — meaning [the curtains of] fine twined linen, as it is written: “And the Tabernacle you shall make of ten curtains of fine twined linen” (Exodus 26:1)! And one can say that [the Gemara] deduced [this] because the verse is written regarding the erection of the Tabernacle, and earlier it lists the order of their erection: that first he placed the sockets, and afterward the boards; and it is written after the boards: “And he spread the tent” — which implies that this refers to the bottom curtains, which are [made of] fine twined linen, as they are [described at] the beginning of the passage. Yet it is [still] puzzling: Why did [the Gemara] not derive [this] from the fact that “Tabernacle” refers to curtains of fine twined linen, as it is written: “And the Tabernacle you shall make...” (Exodus 26:1), and the Tabernacle is called a “tent,” as it is written: “the Tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting” (Exodus 39:32)? And perhaps [the Gemara actually] relied on this verse.

Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:1:2.hebrew: אם כן ג"ש מאי אהני ליה - והא דאמר: "כל פותח טפח מביא את הטומאה" — היינו מק"ו ממצורע, כדיליף בספרי, וכדפיר' בקונטרס. וא"ת: והיכי יליף? נימא דיו כמצורע: שלא יטמא אלא טומאת ערב, ודווקא בעומד או ביושב ולא עובר, כדתניא במסכת נגעים ומייתי לה ובפ"ק דקדושין (ד' לג:): "טמא יושב תחת האילן וטהור עובר — טמא" כו'?! וי"ל: דאינו אלא גילוי מילתא בעלמא מק"ו דמצורע — דלית לן למילף "אהל" "אהל" ממשכן לענין למעט הבאת טומאה בשאר אהלים דלאו פשתן; ולא ילפינן ממשכן אלא לטומאת עצמו, אפילו מחובר, דדוקא פשתן ולא שאר יוצא מן העץ, ולענין אהל שאינו עשוי בידי אדם לרבי יהודה בפ"ב דסוכה (דף כא. ושם) — דלא מצינן למילף ממצורע, ולא אשכחן ביה קרא לא למעט ולא לרבות אהל שאינו עשוי בידי אדם:
Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:1:2.english: "If so, what does the verbal analogy accomplish?" - And that which is said: "Whatever has an opening of a handbreadth brings the impurity" — that is [derived] from an a fortiori argument (kal vachomer) from a metzora, as is derived in the Sifrei and as explained in the Kuntres [Rashi]. And if you say: And how can [the Sifrei] derive [this]? Let us say [the principle of] dayyo [it is sufficient for that which is derived by an a fortiori argument to be like the source from which it is derived] — like a metzora: that it should transmit impurity only until evening, and specifically when standing or sitting, but not when passing through, as is taught in tractate Negaim [13:7] and cited in the first chapter of Kiddushin (33b): "[If] an impure person is sitting under a tree and a pure person passes by, [the pure person] is impure, etc."?! And it can be answered: It is merely a clarification of the matter (giluy milta be'alma) through the a fortiori argument from a metzora — that we are not to derive "tent" "tent" from the Tabernacle to exclude the transmission of impurity in other tents that are not of linen; and we derive from the Tabernacle only with regard to [the tent's] own susceptibility to impurity, even when attached [to the ground], that [it applies] specifically to linen and not to other plant-derived products; and with regard to a tent that is not made by human hands according to Rabbi Yehuda in the second chapter of Sukkah (21a and there), as we cannot derive [that] from a metzora, and we did not find a verse regarding it either to exclude or to include a tent that is not made by human hands.

Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:2:1.hebrew: אי מה להלן קרשים כו' - פירש בקונטרס: דאף עץ יהא קרוי אהל. וקשה לריב"א: דהא דפנות אין קרויות אהל, אלא המכס' שמלמעלה הוא קרוי אהל. ומפ' דה"ק: אי מה להלן קרשים בהדי פשתן — אף כאן בטומאת אהל קרשים בהדי פשתן. ואע"ג דאהל אהל ריבה לענין דלא בעינן שזורים ולכפול ששה, וכן לענין דלא בעינן צמר ופשתים יחד כי התם, אלא אפילו פשתים ולא צמר — מ"מ פריך דליהוי קרשים בהדי פשתים, דסתם אהל קרוי עם הכיסוי ועם הדפנות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:2:1.english: "If [so], just as below [there were] beams, etc." - Rashi explained that wood, too, should be called a tent. And the Riva finds this difficult: For walls are not called a tent; rather, [only] the covering that is above is called a tent. And [the Riva] explains that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: If [so], just as below [there were] beams along with linen, so too here, in [the laws of] tent impurity, [there must be] beams along with linen. And even though [the repetition of] "tent" [and] "tent" amplifies [the definition of a tent] with regard to [the fact] that we do not require [the threads to be] twisted and folded sixfold, and likewise with regard to [the fact] that we do not require wool and linen together as [was the case] there, but rather even linen without wool [suffices] — nevertheless, [the Gemara] challenges that there should be beams along with linen, for an ordinary tent is designated [as such only] with the covering and with the walls.

Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:2:2.hebrew: ואין קרשים קרוים משכן - וקשה לרי: הא כתיב "יהיה סרוח על צדי המשכן מזה ומזה לכסותו", ואמר לקמן בהזורק (שבת דף צח:): "לכסות אמה של קרשים", ואיכא למ"ד: "אמה של אדנים" — אלמא דקרשים איקרי משכן! ויש לומר: דצדי המשכן איקרי, ולא משכן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:2:2.english: "And the beams are not called Tabernacle" - And it is difficult to the Ri: Behold, it is written: "[...it] shall hang over the sides of the Tabernacle on this side and on that side, to cover it" (Exodus 26:13), and [the Gemara] says later on in [the chapter] HaZorek (Shabbat 98b): "[this means] to cover a cubit of the beams," and there is one who says, "[to cover] a cubit of the sockets" — thus implying that the beams are called "Tabernacle"! And one can say: They are called "the sides of the Tabernacle," but not "Tabernacle" [alone].

Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:5:1.hebrew: ריבה עור בהמה טמאה - פירש רבינו שמואל דלהכי איצטריך לרבויי עור בהמה טמאה, כדקתני בת"כ (פ' תזריע): צמר — אין לי אלא מין בהמה דקה ונאכל כו', דומיא דצמר שהוא דוקא של כבשים; מנין לרבות עור בהמה דקה ואין נאכלת, בהמה גסה נאכלת ואין נאכלת, עד שתהא מרבה עורות שרצים? תלמוד לומר: "בעור" "בעור". ונראה, דהא דנקט "בהמה גסה נאכלת" — אגב אחריני נקט, דאיהי לא בעיא קרא; דהא בשמעתין ילפינן לענין טומאת אהל: כל מין טהורה מאילים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:5:1.english: "It amplified [to include] the hide of a non-kosher animal" - Rabbeinu Shmuel explained that for this [reason] it was necessary to include the hide of a non-kosher animal, as it is taught in Torat Kohanim (Parashat Tazria): [From the mention of] "wool," I have [derived] only a species of small animal that is edible [i.e., kosher], etc., similar to wool, which is specifically from sheep; from where [is it derived] to include the hide of a small animal that is not edible [i.e., non-kosher], [and of] a large animal, [whether] edible or not edible, up until one includes the hides of creeping animals? The verse states: "In a hide" [and] "in a hide." And it appears [to Tosafot] that that which [the baraita] mentions "a large edible animal" — it mentions [it] incidentally on account of the others, for it does not require a verse [of its own]; since in our sugya we derive regarding the ritual impurity of a tent [over a corpse] every kosher species from "rams."

Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:5:2.hebrew: ושלקה ביד כהן - מפרש נמי רבינו שמואל דאיצטריך לרבויי, משום דכתיב: "והבגד כי יהיה בו נגע צרעת וגו' והראה אל הכהן" — דמשמע דאם לא היתה בו נגע קודם שהראהו לכהן, טהור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:5:2.english: "And that was afflicted in the hands of a priest" - Rabbeinu Shmuel also explains that it was necessary to include [this], because it is written: "When a garment has an affliction of leprosy in it... and it is shown to the priest" — which implies that if there was no affliction in it before he showed it to the priest, [it is] pure.

Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:5:3.hebrew: שכן שתי וערב טמא בהן - מה שאין כן במת, כדנפקא לן בפרק במה אשה (לקמן שבת דף סד.):
Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:5:3.english: "As warp and woof become ritually impure in them" - Which is not the case regarding a corpse, as is derived for us in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Isha (below, Shabbat 64a).

Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:6:1.hebrew: אלא גמר משרצים דתניא עור אין לי אלא עור של בהמה טהורה - וא"ת: מנלן דאיירי קרא בעור בהמה טהורה? ויש לומר: כמו בנגעים, דהכא כתיב "שק", וה"א: מה שק מין בהמה דקה ונאכל — כדמוכח בת"כ ולקמן דשק הוי דבר הבא מן העזים — אף עור מין בהמה דקה ונאכל. אע"ג דבת"כ מרבה אף שק הבא מחזיר, שהוא דבר טמא — אפ"ה הוה אמינא: דלא הוקשה עור אלא למשמעות דשק, דהיינו של עזים, ולא הוקש למאי דמרבי בשק; לכך איצטריך ריבוי. — הרב פורת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:6:1.english: Rather, he derived it from creeping animals, as it was taught: "Hide" — I have only the hide of a kosher animal - And if you say: From where do we know that the verse is speaking of the hide of a kosher animal? One can say: Just as regarding leprosy afflictions, for here [too] it is written "sack". And I would have said: Just as "sack" is [made from] a species of small animal that may be eaten — as is proven in Torat Kohanim and later [in the Gemara] that "sack" is something that comes from goats — so too "hide" [would be limited to] a species of small animal that may be eaten. Even though in Torat Kohanim it includes even a sack that comes from a pig, which is a non-kosher thing, even so, I would have said that "hide" was juxtaposed only to the primary meaning of "sack" — which is of goats — and was not juxtaposed to that which is included in "sack"; therefore, an inclusion was necessary. — Rabbi Porat.

Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:6:2.hebrew: מה לשרצים - וליכא למיפרך: שיטמא מת בכעדשה מק"ו — דהא כל שיעורים הם הלכה למשה מסיני. וקשה לר"י: ונילף מת משרצים בגזירה שוה דבגד ועור, כדאמר לקמן בפרק במה אשה (ג"ז שם)? ואומר ר"י: משום דג"ש דאהל אהל ממשכן סתרה לה, לכך איצטריך ריבוי. ועוד י"ל: דג"ש לא איירי בטומאת אהל [המת] עצמו המחובר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 28a:6:2.english: "What [is the comparison] to creeping animals" - And one cannot refute [the Gemara's premise by arguing] that a corpse should impart impurity with [a piece as small as] a lentil-bulk via an a fortiori argument [kal va-chomer] — for all [halakhic] measurements are a Halakhah to Moses from Sinai. And the Ri raises a difficulty: Why not derive [the laws of] a corpse from creeping animals via the verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah] of "garment and hide," as [the Gemara] says later in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Isha (this too is there)? And the Ri says: Because the verbal analogy of "tent" [and] "tent" from the Tabernacle contradicts it; therefore, an amplification was necessary. And furthermore it can be said: The verbal analogy does not deal with the impurity of the tent [of the corpse] itself when attached [as a covering].
